concerns.concern: The velocity anomaly rests on only seven temperature points, with no data between 150 and 200 K. The drop at T_N is inferred from two points 50 K apart, and one of them (150 K) is already below T_N.
concerns.quote: There are no data between 150 and 200 K. The "drop at T_N" is therefore inferred from two points 50 K apart

concerns.concern: The quoted 5.5% drop is measured from a single 200 K maximum. Relative to 300 K the AFM-phase velocity is only about 2.7% lower, so the size of the anomaly is not established. The anomaly should be quoted against a fitted paramagnetic background.
concerns.quote: The quoted 5.5% (1920 → 1815 m s⁻¹) is measured from the single 200 K maximum.

concerns.concern: Room-temperature velocities disagree between Fig. 3 (~1950 m/s) and Fig. 4 (~1865 m/s) by about 4%. This is comparable to the claimed effect and points to systematic errors from angle calibration, spot position, cryostat windows or fitting.
concerns.quote: this ~4% run-to-run (or setup-to-setup) discrepancy is of the same order as the 5.5% anomaly

concerns.concern: Adsorbate or ice condensation (mass loading) on cooling could lower the surface-wave velocity. It would also explain the loss of peak intensity and the rising background at 80–90 K. Cryostat type and vacuum level are not reported.
concerns.quote: Adsorbate/ice condensation (mass loading). This is a textbook SAW-velocity-lowering effect.

concerns.concern: Thermal drift of the sample tilt or cold finger could change the scattering angle and hence q. Velocity is computed with a nominal q on a dispersive mode, so drift would shift the apparent velocity.
concerns.quote: Drift changes θ, and hence q, while v is computed with a nominal q.

concerns.concern: Laser heating during BMS is uncontrolled and unreported, typically at mW powers. The actual flake temperature and the apparent location of T_N are therefore uncertain.
concerns.quote: BMS laser power and spot size are not given.

concerns.concern: Thermal-expansion mismatch between the flake and the SiO₂/Si substrate could cause strain, partial delamination or interfacial slip on cooling. Any of these would lower the effective velocity without a magnetic cause.
concerns.quote: can produce strain, partial delamination or interfacial slip on cooling, all of which lower the effective velocity.

concerns.concern: There is no internal reference at each temperature to calibrate q and expose drift, such as a substrate mode or the Si Brillouin peak. There is also no non-magnetic control flake and no second magnet with a different T_N to show that the anomaly tracks magnetic order.
concerns.quote: Measure FePS₃ (T_N ≈ 118 K) or MnPS₃ (T_N ≈ 78 K) and show that the anomaly tracks each material's T_N.

concerns.concern: The DFT+FEM calculation gives only a 0.54% shift, an order of magnitude below the measured ~5.5%. The abstract's claim that theory reproduces the magnetic-order-induced shift is therefore overstated.
concerns.quote: The calculated shift is 0.54% (4.603 → 4.578 GHz), an order of magnitude below the measured 5.5%

concerns.concern: The Rayleigh velocity is controlled mainly by c33 and c44, yet the DFT shows c44 unchanged and c22 increasing. The calculation therefore does not identify the mechanism the experiment implies.
concerns.quote: The DFT therefore does not identify the mechanism the experiment implies, namely a sizable reduction of the out-of-plane and shear constants.

concerns.concern: The text emphasizes the 17% change in c66, but c66 governs shear-horizontal motion, not the Rayleigh wave in this propagation geometry.
concerns.quote: The text's emphasis on c₆₆ (+17%) is not relevant here.

concerns.concern: The DFT omits a Hubbard U, which Ni²⁺ d⁸ states require, and AFM–NM differences in cij are likely U-sensitive. The authors should also show whether plain PBE even yields zigzag order as the lowest-energy state.
concerns.quote: No Hubbard U. Ni²⁺ d⁸ states require one.

concerns.concern: Using the non-magnetic state as a proxy for the paramagnetic phase conflates moment formation with long-range ordering, because local S=1 moments persist above T_N. Competing orderings or disordered-local-moment configurations would be better comparisons.
concerns.quote: The NM state is a poor proxy for the PM phase. In the PM phase, local S = 1 moments persist

concerns.concern: The authors should use the sensitivity analysis to invert the measurement. They should state what fractional change in c44 and/or c33 is needed to produce the observed velocity change, and discuss whether it is plausible.
concerns.quote: the authors should invert the measurement. They should state what fractional change in c₄₄, c₃₃, or a combination, is needed

concerns.concern: The 11% elastic-constant estimate assumes v ∝ √(c/ρ) for the film alone. That is invalid for a dispersive film/substrate mode, as the authors' own FEM shows, and it should be replaced by an FEM-based inversion.
concerns.quote: That does not hold for a dispersive film/substrate mode with substantial substrate participation.

concerns.concern: The velocity change could be strain-mediated rather than intrinsic: magnetostriction plus substrate clamping would act through acoustoelastic third-order constants. This is not considered, and relevant nanomechanical-resonator work (Šiškins et al. 2020) is not cited.
concerns.quote: these produce a change in biaxial strain, which can shift the velocity through third-order (acoustoelastic) constants independently of any change in cᵢⱼ.

concerns.concern: There is no reproducibility check: no cooling-and-warming runs to test for hysteresis, and measurements on only one flake.
concerns.quote: Record both cooling and warming runs to check reproducibility and hysteresis. Measure at least two further flakes.

concerns.concern: The angle uncertainty is not quantified or propagated into q and v. It is also not stated whether Fig. 3 was measured in the cryostat.
concerns.quote: Quantify the uncertainty in θ and propagate it into q and v.

concerns.concern: The ~3% velocity increase from 300 to 200 K is large for anharmonic stiffening alone. It may already contain contributions from short-range magnetic correlations above T_N.
concerns.quote: The 300 → 200 K increase of ~3% is large for anharmonic stiffening alone.

concerns.concern: The origin of the ±10–25 m/s error bars is not reported. It is unclear whether they are fit errors only or repeat-measurement scatter.
concerns.quote: Report the error budget behind the ±10–25 m s⁻¹ bars. Are these fit errors only, or repeat-measurement scatter?

concerns.concern: The model c_eff = c⁽⁰⁾ − λ²χ predicts a cusp that recovers below T_N, but the data show a persistent step. A Landau model coupling strain to L² is the appropriate framework.
concerns.quote: The form c_eff = c⁽⁰⁾ − λ²χ_m predicts a cusp or dip near T_N that recovers below it. The data show a persistent step.

concerns.concern: The optical-phonon shift is written with the first derivative of the exchange, ∂J/∂u. The standard result involves the second derivative, ∂²J/∂u².
concerns.quote: The standard result (Granado et al., Lockwood and Cottam) involves ∂²J/∂u².

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic energy used is a single-ion/anisotropic form, but it is invoked as exchange striction.
concerns.quote: E_me = −Σ B_αβ ε_αβ S_α S_β is a single-ion/anisotropic form, but it is invoked as exchange striction.

concerns.concern: The claimed distinction is overstated: exchange-striction contributions to cij also scale with short-range spin correlations. The authors should explain why acoustic waves would be sensitive specifically to long-range order and not to correlations that persist above T_N.
concerns.quote: Exchange-striction contributions to cᵢⱼ also scale with ⟨Sᵢ·Sⱼ⟩, plus fluctuation terms.

concerns.concern: The roughly 60° cleavage edges do not uniquely identify the a-axis in a pseudo-hexagonal lattice. This matters for zigzag order, and the axes should be confirmed, for example by polarized Raman.
concerns.quote: an edge alone does not uniquely identify the a-axis.

concerns.concern: Zigzag magnetic domains within the laser spot are not discussed.
concerns.quote: They should discuss zigzag domains within the laser spot.

concerns.concern: No measurement with q along the a-axis was made. Such a measurement would test whether the anomaly shows the anisotropy expected from zigzag order.
concerns.quote: A measurement with q along a would test whether the anomaly carries the anisotropy expected from zigzag order.

concerns.concern: The magnetic-structure description is inconsistent. The paper says interlayer coupling is antiferromagnetic while quoting k=[010], which in the C2/m cell implies ferromagnetic interlayer stacking.
concerns.quote: For the C2/m cell, k = [010] corresponds to ferromagnetic interlayer stacking (Wildes et al., 2015).

concerns.concern: The interlayer magnetic configuration used in the DFT supercell is not specified. This matters because c33 and c44 are the interlayer-sensitive constants.
concerns.quote: specify the interlayer magnetic configuration used in the 1×4×2 DFT supercell

concerns.concern: The Raman anharmonic fits appear to span the whole temperature range, including below T_N. They should be fitted above T_N only and extrapolated below.
concerns.quote: the anharmonic fits appear to span the whole temperature range, including below T_N.

concerns.concern: No anharmonic fits are shown for the Raman FWHM, yet a 0.3 cm⁻¹ deviation is quoted. Fig. 2d visibly shows an FWHM step near T_N.
concerns.quote: Figs. 2d–e show no anharmonic fits, yet the text quotes a 0.3 cm⁻¹ deviation.

concerns.concern: The previously reported splitting of the ~176 cm⁻¹ mode is absent. This may reflect resolution, polarization geometry or thickness, and the spectral resolution is not stated.
concerns.quote: The absence of the splitting reported by Kim et al. may reflect spectral resolution, grating, polarization geometry, or flake thickness.

concerns.concern: Claiming that 0.024 mW was used to ensure high signal-to-noise is contradictory given the very low power. Integration times should be clarified.
concerns.quote: Saying that 0.024 mW was used "to ensure a high signal-to-noise ratio" is at odds with such low power.

concerns.concern: The general claim that optical phonons are insensitive to magnetic order should be moderated, given prior reports of magnetic signatures in NiPS₃ Raman spectra.
concerns.quote: moderate the general claim that optical phonons are insensitive

concerns.concern: The non-magnetic simulation gives about 10% higher frequency than measured at room temperature. This offset exceeds the effect under study.
concerns.quote: a ~10% offset that exceeds the effect under study.

concerns.concern: Key FEM inputs are not reported. These include NiPS₃ density in each phase, substrate constants, how the monoclinic tensor was rotated and its sign conventions, and thickness uniformity within the spot.
concerns.quote: how the monoclinic tensor was rotated into the FEM frame (c vs. c*, sign conventions for c₁₅, c₂₅, c₃₅, c₄₆)

concerns.concern: The sensitivity of the velocity to flake thickness is not shown, although thickness uncertainty directly shifts the dispersive mode.
concerns.quote: Thickness uncertainty directly shifts the dispersive mode. The sensitivity of v to h should be shown.

concerns.concern: Low-temperature peaks are weak and broad on a sloping background. Fits with residuals, the background model and linewidth versus temperature should be shown; a linewidth anomaly would support a magnetic origin.
concerns.quote: show the fits with residuals, the background model, and the linewidth versus temperature.

concerns.concern: The marked decrease in peak intensity on cooling is not discussed, and condensation is a possible cause.
concerns.quote: The marked intensity decrease on cooling should be discussed

concerns.concern: A ~220 nm flake is effectively bulk, so the discussion of the strict 2D limit and Mermin–Wagner is not tested by this work.
concerns.quote: A ~220 nm flake (~330 layers) is effectively bulk.

concerns.concern: Several-percent elastic anomalies at magnetic transitions are well documented in 3D antiferromagnets. "Giant" and "rarely reported" should be justified quantitatively or tempered.
concerns.quote: "Giant" and "rarely reported" should be justified quantitatively, e.g., with a magnetoelastic coupling constant compared against literature values, or tempered.

concerns.concern: The anomaly is quoted inconsistently as ~5.5% and ~6%, and the drop is placed at 150 K while T_N is ~155 K.
concerns.quote: The anomaly is quoted as both "~5.5%" and "~6%" (pp. 15, 17)

concerns.concern: The axes of Fig. 2a are mislabeled. They should be Raman shift and intensity.
concerns.quote: The x-axis is labeled "Temperature (K)" and the y-axis "Raman Shift (cm⁻¹)".

concerns.concern: There are typos and a wrong term: "Temperaure", "REFRENCES", and "electrodynamic" where "elastodynamic" is meant.
concerns.quote: "linear electrodynamic equation" should read "elastodynamic".

concerns.concern: The supercell label 1×4×2 is inconsistent with the stated lattice dimensions. Relaxed lattice parameters for both phases, compared with experiment, are missing.
concerns.quote: Please reconcile the labeling and state the relaxed lattice parameters for both phases compared with experiment.

concerns.concern: BMS experimental details are missing: laser power, spot size, collection aperture and q-resolution, free spectral range, acquisition time, cryostat model and vacuum.
concerns.quote: Missing BMS experimental details

concerns.concern: The statement of the Loudon selection rule is imprecise. Since NiPS₃ absorbs at 532 nm, the absorption depth and the role of the elasto-optic contribution should be stated.
concerns.quote: state the absorption depth and whether the elasto-optic contribution matters.

concerns.concern: Temperature ranges are inconsistent: Raman methods say 77–300 K but Fig. 2 shows 90–290 K, and the 80 K BMS spectrum is absent from Fig. 4b.
concerns.quote: The Raman methods state 77–300 K, but Fig. 2 shows 90–290 K.

concerns.concern: The key sensitivity results should be moved into the main text, because the interpretation rests on them.
concerns.quote: Move the key sensitivity results (Supp. Table 2) into the main text

concerns.concern: Full dispersion should be measured in both phases and along two directions, so that FEM inversion can determine which elastic constants change and by how much.
concerns.quote: Take f(q) at, e.g., 200 K and 90 K, with q along both a and b.
